title: transparent shadow capture with lag compaction and atomic swap
author: Nina Kapoor
description: Motivation: Shadow traffic is an essential signal for validating new model variants without affecting production responses, but existing shadow capture leaves a gap: when worker lag increases (slow downstream KV writes, network backpressure), shadow frames are dropped or stored incompletely leading to noisy replay and misleading metrics. This PR introduces a transparent shadow capture pipeline with lag compaction and an atomic swap path for canary handoffs so that shadow replays are deterministic and can be used directly for automated A/B gating and rollback decisions. Summary of changes: 1) shadow capture layer: non-intrusive middleware that forks in-flight requests to a compacted write-ahead buffer; captures full request metadata, prompt prefixes, routing tags, and KV-cache deltas; uses schema-v2 envelope for forward/backward compatibility; 2) lag compactor: background compaction job that coalesces batches from slow backends, dropping/annotating only strictly redundant intermediate states (configurable TTL and tolerance); 3) atomic swap adapter: when a canary passes validation, the adapter can flip serving plane traffic via commit log pointer update (atomic pointer swap) rather than gradual rebinds, preserving session stickiness and avoiding double-processing; 4) observability & safety: new metrics (shadow_capture_lag_ms, compaction_coalesced_ops, swap_commit_latency_ms), distributed trace spans and per-request sampling hooks; 5) rollout integration: new rollout strategy type "shadow-verify-and-atomic-swap" for Console and API with default safety gates (latency SLO, quality delta threshold, error budget check); 6) tests & CI: unit coverage for compactor heuristics, integration harness that replays captured shadows into a canary instance and compares deterministic outputs against golden prompt sets. Migration notes: capture pipeline uses schema-v2 but falls back to schema-v1 if peer components not upgraded; compaction parameters default to conservative values (min_ttl=15s, max_coalesce=50) to avoid premature trimming in low-traffic environments. Rollout playbook: 1) enable shadow capture on a subset of routes; 2) run shadow-verify for 24h with session-affine sampling; 3) evaluate metrics dashboard produced by this PR's recorder; 4) on pass, invoke atomic swap via Console or API to commit canary. Safety: atomic swap is gated behind an explicit commit call and requires both latency and quality gates to be green; rollback is supported via swap-rewind which replays a snapshot of the previous commit pointer and issues a graceful drain. Backwards compatibility: changes are additive; older agents ignore the new envelope and compactor is no-op if not enabled. Related work: follows on ideas from ENG-4109 (shadow-replay-stability) and complements rollout-simulator work for deterministic playback. Checklist: - [x] design doc and API sketch attached - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] dashboards and alert rules - [x] migration + playbook - [x] docs for Console surface and SDK example - [x] staged canary run and observed stable metrics (internal test cluster)

review_comments: Ava Martinez (2026-02-22): Nice end-to-end. Two questions: what is the expected memory impact of the write-ahead buffer under a sustained 10x traffic spike? Can compaction be back-pressured to disk?

Author Nina Kapoor (2026-02-22): We cap in-memory buffer by route with a hard limit (configurable per-namespace) and spill-to-disk is supported via the spill_path flag; added config docs and default limit=64MB/route in k8s overlay.
Samir Patel (2026-02-24): The atomic swap is neat but I'm concerned about race between swap commit and in-flight session-affine requests. Can we add a short drain window?
Author Nina Kapoor (2026-02-24): Implemented a 500ms default drain-window and a tunable parameter; added test for partial-swap failure and retry path. See orchestrator/swap/swap_test.go commit.

Li Chen (2026-02-26): Integration tests flaky on mac runner (timeout in compactor tests). CI rerun fixed it but please ensure timeouts are parameterized. Also please add a note for ops to tune compactor TTL for low traffic customers.
Author Nina Kapoor (2026-02-27): Parameterized test timeouts and updated docs/rollouts/atomic_swap_playbook.md with ops tuning section.
release_notes: Added transparent shadow capture pipeline with lag compaction and atomic swap rollout strategy. Provides deterministic shadow replay for A/B gating and a new atomic commit path for canary promotion. Configurable compaction defaults to conservative settings to avoid data loss. Operators should review compactor TTL and memory spill settings before enabling broadly.
